title: Bang-Bang
intro: The particle sits in the ground state of trap A. Deliver it to the ground state of trap B, 12 units away, and quickly. The target is not a place but a state: the observation asks "is the particle in the ground state of B?" and says yes with probability |⟨B₀|ψ⟩|². Switching straight from A to B makes it slosh through B forever. A third trap halfway between, held for exactly half an oscillation period, swings the particle over and parks it at rest.
goal: Move the particle from trap A to the ground state of trap B (the dashed ring), then observe. Keys 1, 2, 3 switch traps A, M (the midpoint) and B on and off.

physics.point: In a harmonic trap every packet swings with the same period. Started at rest at one turning point, it arrives at rest at the other after exactly half a period: put that turning point on B.

idea: Moving trapped atoms or ions from one place to another is a routine job in quantum technology. Moving the trap slowly (adiabatically) keeps the particle in the ground state, but takes a long time, and the particle meanwhile decoheres. A shortcut to adiabaticity reaches the same final state in a finite time.

The simplest shortcut is bang-bang control. Switch from trap A to a trap M halfway to B. The particle, at rest at A, is now at a turning point of M's oscillation, so it swings across and arrives at the other turning point, which is B, at rest, after half a period. Switch to trap B at that moment and it stays there, in B's ground state.

The target here is a quantum state, not a region: the measurement is the projector onto B's ground state |B₀⟩. Once the particle is in trap B the probability |⟨B₀|ψ⟩|² is constant (B₀ is a stationary state of B), so after a good switch you can observe whenever you like, and after a bad one waiting does not help.
maths: In a harmonic trap of frequency ω every coherent state moves like a classical particle: x(t) = x_M + (x₀ − x_M) cos ωt. Starting at rest at x_A, the packet reaches x_B = 2x_M − x_A at t = π/ω, again at rest, and its width is unchanged because the ground states of A, M and B all have σ₀ = 1/√(2ω).
A coherent state displaced by δx with velocity δv relative to B₀ has fidelity
Switching straight from A to B leaves δx = 12: |α|² = 0.4·144/2 ≈ 29 and F ≈ 10⁻¹³. Missing the half period by δt gives δv ≈ ω·6·ωδt, which costs about half the fidelity at δt ≈ 0.6.
Here ω = 0.4, so τ = π/ω ≈ 7.85. The traps are harmonic out to R = 8 and flat beyond (the edge costs about 4% of the fidelity).
try: Press 1 and 3 together at the start: the particle sloshes through B at full speed and the fidelity stays at zero.
Press 1 and 2 at t = 0, then 2 and 3 at t ≈ 7.85: the fidelity jumps to about 96% and stays there.
Switch at t = 7 or t = 9 instead and watch the P_T line settle lower: the leftover velocity is a coherent sloshing in B that never damps.
